issues.what: Chapters 2, 3 and 7 are all titled 'The Convict's Letter'; ch4 'Mr. Fellows' and ch6 'The Rochester Constable' do not fit their chapters

Silas Venn's timeline contradicts itself: transported when she was an infant (ch6, ch7 'three days old') yet 'transported in twenty nine' (ch5), and never tied to the ironed convict Joby fed in ch2, which the brief requires
issues.quote: I was transported for forgery in twenty nine

issues.what: Hester's account says she walked out with a clerk of Fellows's; ch6 says she married Venn, a smith. Ch7 reads her wrist scars as irons, ch8 says a laundry mangle
issues.quote: walked out with a clerk who copied for Mr Fellows

issues.what: Letter muddle: Joby's lodging holds letters 'in my own hand returned unopened' tied with her blue thread; she says she never read them though ch2-3 she read them; the April letter is quoted with two different texts in ch7 and ch8
issues.quote: in my own hand returned unopened

issues.what: Ages: engagement at twenty (ch4) and the ending weeks later, yet ch8 says 'I am twenty four' and 'When I was twenty two I danced'; Joby 'older than twenty four' at 22
issues.quote: I am twenty four and I know my own mind

issues.what: Miss Sallow says she stopped the clocks the night of Clemency's birth; ch1 and ch8 say they stopped at the jilting, before she was born; 'thirty years' kept ten years later
issues.quote: I stopped every clock that night for you

issues.what: Trant's house moves from Portman Square to Half Moon Street; Joby's lodgings move from over a tailor by the Temple to Cursitor Street over a stationer's
issues.quote: The house in Half Moon Street kept its hours.

issues.what: Anachronism: the Thames Embankment was not built until the 1860s
issues.quote: We walked back along the Embankment in silence.

issues.what: 'Rhynes' is Somerset marsh vocabulary, not Kent; the wedding table room is morning room, parlour and wedding room by turns
issues.quote: The mist came up from the rhynes

issues.what: Repeated phrasing and recap: 'hated myself through every quadrille' in ch7 and ch8, 'I read it four times' three times, the ball re-told twice in ch8
issues.quote: I hated myself through every quadrille

issues.what: Brief fidelity: the story compresses 1832-1836 into one spring, so Clemency ends at twenty, not twenty-four; accepted rather than rewritten
issues.quote: When I was twenty two I danced with Harle

fix: Retitle ch2-8. Ch5-6: Venn in the hulks off Chatham, escaped the autumn she was 14 (the ch2 convict Joby fed), recaptured and transported in '26; allowance 'these two years'. Ch7: Hester married Venn the smith; scars not irons; the clocks stopped at the jilting. Ch6: the lodging bundle is Joby's unsent letters; she read only the first two sent. Ch4/8: ages 20/22, forty years. Unify Portman Square, Temple lodgings, morning room; remove the Embankment, rhynes and repeats.
praise: A cool, exact first-person voice that really does thaw, with a card-table opening in ch1 that is as cruel and alive as anything in the batch.
